newsitem.title: USA: Barnes & Noble more aggressive on-line - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Barnes & Noble more aggressive on-line - WSJ.

text.p: Barnes & Noble Inc is becoming more aggressive in its fight to win on-line book buyers from Amazon.com, the Wall Street Journal reported in its "Heard on the Street" column.
In Friday's electronic edition, the paper said that Barnes & Noble has shown a willingness in recent months to use hardball tactics in its battle with Amazon.com.

The giant book retailer recently sued Amazon.com for claiming to be the world's largest bookstore and has offered deep discounts on books that are proving expensive for Amazon.com to match, the paper said.
In addition, Barnes & Noble is negotiating more alliances that will give its Internet business more exposure, according to the Journal.
While Amazon.com still has about a two-year lead over rivals, the company is expected to spend more to fight Barnes & Noble, analysts said.
People close to Amazon.com said the company may even have to borrow money or issue more stock, the paper reported.
Amazon.com's stock closed down 5/8 Thursday at 28-3/4, while Barnes & Noble's stock fell 3/4 to 50.
